_comment: Curated corrections to the aliases derived from CPE strings. Derivation gets the common cases
right and cannot settle ambiguity, so this file is where a human decision is recorded. It is
data, committed and reviewable, so a wrong call here can be found and fixed by anyone.
add: extra needles for a product. Use when the display name shares no words with the CPE.
'Java 8 Update 481' is Oracle's JRE, but the word 'java' appears in no Oracle CPE product
name, so without this it binds to ibm:java - a real finding attributed to the wrong vendor.
drop: needles to remove from a product. Use when a derived needle is too broad and steals names
Every entry needs a reason. An unexplained mapping here is indistinguishable from a typo.
exclude: display-name needles that must bind to NOTHING. Some installs are components of a
product rather than the product: an add-in or a virtual printer carries its OWN version,
so comparing it against the parent product's CVE ranges is meaningless in both
directions. This cannot be expressed as an alias, because word-subset matching has no
way to say 'not this', so the consumers check it separately.

reasons.oracle:jre: Oracle ships as 'Java 8 Update NNN'; no Oracle CPE product contains the word java.
reasons.ibm:java: The bare needle 'java' captured Oracle's Java on a real machine. IBM's JDK identifies itself as 'IBM SDK' or 'Semeru', so it loses nothing.
reasons.chaos_tool_suite_project:ctools: A Drupal module. 'CTools' on Windows is something else entirely; the bare needle only ever produces a wrong match.
reasons.exclude: Components, not products. Their version is the component's, not the parent's, so any comparison against the parent's CVE ranges is meaningless. Measured on a real machine: the Teams Meeting Add-in at 1.26.20101 collected 10 Teams CVEs, and the OneNote virtual printer at 1.0.0.0 collected 6.
